title: Bellarmine's second route: proper latria per accidents—yet do not tell the people images are owed latria
source_text: LVIII. Praeterea docet imaginem Christi adorari posse latria, non improprie tantum, sed etiam proprie, verum per accidens, non per se: ut si quis Christum adoret, prout objective in sua imagine relucet, ut ipsum sic repraesentatum, & quasi vestitum imagine veneretur. Tunc enim necessario adorari imaginem eodem cultu quo Christum ipsum; quoniam imago concipitur eo tempore conjuncta cum exemplari quod adoratur: qui autem adorat aliquem, adorat etiam omnia quae cum illo conjuncta sunt; sicut qui adorat Regem vestitum, adorat simul Regem & vestes. Sed adorationem illam esse per accidens, non per se: quia, in eo casu imago nec est ipsum suppositum quod adoratur, nec ratio adorationis, sed quiddam adjunctum. Existimat autem Bellarminus prohibitum quidem imaginem colere latria proprie & per se, non tamen illam latria colere improprie, vel per accidens. Quoniam tamen non debet simpliciter affirmari, id quod verum est solum improprie, vel per accidens, idcirco non vult dicendum esse imaginibus deberi cultum latriae, sed contrarium potius, praesertim si sermo ad populum habeatur. De Ecclesia triumphante lib. 2. cap. 22. & 23.
pass_a_gloss: Besides he teaches that the image of Christ can be adored with latria, not only improperly, but also properly, yet per accidents, not per se: as if someone should adore Christ as he objectively shines forth in his image, so as to venerate him thus represented and as it were clothed with the image. For then the image is necessarily adored with the same cult as Christ himself; because the image is conceived at that time joined with the exemplar that is adored: but he who adores someone also adores all things that are joined with him; just as he who adores a clothed King adores at once the King and the garments. But that that adoration is per accidents, not per se: because, in that case the image is neither the very subject that is adored, nor the reason of adoration, but something adjunct. But Bellarmine judges that it is indeed forbidden to cultivate an image with latria properly and per se, yet not to cultivate it with latria improperly, or per accidents. Yet because that which is true only improperly, or per accidents, ought not to be simply affirmed, therefore he does not wish it to be said that the cult of latria is owed to images, but rather the contrary, especially if speech is had to the people. On the Triumphant Church, book 2, chapters 22 and 23.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine's second route: proper latria per accidents—Christ adored as shining in the image, like king-plus-clothes.
Latria per se to the image remains forbidden; yet he forbids telling the people that images are owed latria, preferring the contrary for popular speech (II.22-23).

choices.english: as it were clothed with the image
